pad.title: Buffs
pad.help.body:
# What the mod does
Casts buffs **in groups** with one button. It picks the caster, spends the spell slots and skips anyone who already has the buff.
@pad Everything is set up in this menu with the gamepad.
@kb Everything is set up in this menu with the keyboard; with mouse and keyboard, the quick cast bar casts a group in one click.
How it works:
1. Pick a group or create your own — a set of buffs for one situation.
2. Add buffs to it. The mod decides who receives them.
3. Tick the buffs to cast.
4. Cast: press {A} on a group in the Cast tab, or click its button on the quick cast bar.

# Opening the menu
- **Gamepad** — the buff card in the game's menu, after the game's own cards.
- **Mouse and keyboard** — the last button of the quick cast bar above the action bar.
- Start or [[Esc]] opens the game's menu over the buff menu; the buff menu returns afterwards.

# Keyboard
While the menu is open, the game's own keys do nothing. Every gamepad button has a key near WASD:
- [[W]] [[A]] [[S]] [[D]] or the arrow keys — move; hold to repeat.
- [[E]], [[Enter]] or [[Space]] — confirm (gamepad A).
- [[Q]] or [[Backspace]] — back (gamepad B); on a tab, close the menu.
- [[Esc]] (gamepad Start) — the game's menu over the buff menu; the buff menu returns afterwards.
- [[R]] — gamepad X, [[F]] — gamepad Y.
- [[X]] / [[C]] or [[PgUp]] / [[PgDn]] — gamepad LB / RB: the neighbouring tab.
- [[Del]] — delete your own group in the Groups tab (asks first). [[Home]] / [[End]] — first and last row.
- [[1]]–[[9]] in the Cast tab — cast the group with that number.
Hints and help show keys or gamepad buttons depending on the game's control mode; to choose manually, use Settings › "Hints".

# Mouse
The mouse works in the menu in either hint mode; on the Steam Deck it is the right trackpad. While the menu is open, clicks do not reach the game, so the party does not move.
- **Hovering** highlights a row, a key or a hint; the selection stays where it is.
- **Left click** on a row selects it; a second click on the selected row does what {A} does. This way a group in the Cast tab is never cast by accident: the first click only selects it.
- **A single click** acts at once on: the tab names at the top and the {LB}{RB} icons next to them; "Buffing in combat"; "+ New group"; a buff's tick box; a party member at the bottom of the Buffs tab and the "Show" value there; the keys of the on-screen keyboard; the switches and the arrows of choices in Settings (click the side of a switch you want).
- **Right click** — back, like {B}; on a tab, it closes the menu.
- **The wheel** scrolls group buffs, buff targets, settings and help; the selection moves with the list.
- **The hints at the bottom** can be clicked and do what their button or key does: Close, Rename, Fill by duration and so on. For an {LB}{RB} pair, click the icon of the side you want.

# Quick cast bar
With mouse and keyboard, a row of buttons is shown above the action bar: one for each group in the Cast tab, numbered as in the menu, followed by a button that opens the menu.
- **Left click** — cast the group; the result pops up at the top of the screen.
- **Right click** — all buffs of the group.
- Hover — the group's name and buffs.
In combat, the group buttons are locked unless "Buffing in combat" is on. With the gamepad there is no bar: the menu opens from its card.

# Tabs
The menu has tabs: Cast, Buffs, Groups, Settings, Help. {LB}{RB} — the neighbouring tab; with the mouse, click a name. {B} on a tab closes the menu.
Tabs open nested pages: a group's buffs, a group's name, the targets of a buff from a group, a buff's settings. There {B} goes back to the tab, and {LB}{RB} serve the page itself.

# Cast
{UP}{DOWN}| select a row.
{A}| on a group — cast it; on "Buffing in combat" — switch it on or off.
{X}| cast all shown groups one after another.
{B}| close the menu.
## Group row
- **buffs N** — ticked buffs in the group.
- **active A/B** — how many of the intended targets have the buff. Yellow — something has worn off, green — everything is in place.
- **next expires** — time left on the shortest one.
- **off N** — unticked buffs in the group.
## Buffing in combat
{A} allows groups to be cast during combat. Off by default.

# Groups
A group is a set of buffs cast with one command. A group without its own name is named after its **duration** — the main property of a group, used by fill by duration.
## Built-in — cannot be deleted
- "{G1}" — after resting, long-lasting.
- "{G2}" — before a dangerous place.
- "{G3}" — right before a boss fight.
A built-in group can be renamed, given a different duration and hidden from the Cast tab, but not deleted.
## Your own groups
Up to 12, e.g. "Against undead" or "Fire protection". Your own groups can be deleted.
## Groups tab
{UP}{DOWN}| select a group.
{A}| open the group's buffs. On "+ New group" — create a group.
{Y}| rename and change the duration.
{X}| hide or show in the Cast tab. A hidden group is not cast by {X} there, but can be set up as usual.
{R3}| hold — delete your own group; it asks first: {A} — delete, {B} — cancel. The hint shows on your own groups only. Buffs that were only in this group lose their targets; in other groups they stay as they were.
{B}| close the menu.
## Name and duration
@pad The name is typed on the on-screen keyboard:
@pad {UP}{DOWN}| and {LEFT}{RIGHT} — select a key.
@pad {A}| type the letter. "Aa" — capitals, "EN/RU" — layout.
@pad {X}| erase a letter.
@pad {LB}{RB}| change the group's duration.
@pad {Y}| done. {B} — cancel.
@kb Type the name on the keyboard: [[Enter]] — done, [[Backspace]] — erase, [[PgUp]] / [[PgDn]] — duration, [[Backspace]] on an empty name or the right mouse button — cancel.
An empty name means the group is named after its duration.
@pad The Steam keyboard (Steam + X) works too.

# Group buffs
Open: {A} on a group in the group list.
At the top — the group's buffs, each with a tick box. Below, in grey — all other buffs of the party, those matching the group's duration first.
Columns: name · duration · targeting (self, party, 1 performer) · targets: set / possible.
{UP}{DOWN}| select a buff.
{A}| add the buff to the group or remove it.
{X}| tick or untick.
{Y}| fill by duration — see the next section.
{RIGHT}| open the buff's targets.
{RB}| buff settings: combat start, sources, casters.
{B}| back.
##SRC##
## The tick
An unticked buff is off **in this group only**: it stays in the list, keeps its targets and still works in other groups. Tick it again and it is cast again. Handy for spare buffs, without losing their setup.
## Adding and removing
- An added buff is ticked and gets targets automatically (see "Who gets the buff").
- If nobody in the current party can receive the buff, it is not added.
- A buff can be in several groups. Removed from one, it stays in the others.
- Removed from its last group, it loses its targets.

# Fill by duration
The main way to fill a group. {Y} in group buffs finds every buff your party can cast and adds those that match the group's duration.
## What exactly happens
- It goes through every buff the mod found in the party: spellbook spells, class abilities, activatable abilities and songs.
- It takes only buffs of the group's duration (see the list below).
- They are added **unticked** — nothing is cast until you tick what you need with {X}.
- A buff without targets gets them automatically: self, party or one performer. If the buff already has targets (it is in another group), they are kept — targets are shared by all groups the buff is in.
- Buffs already in the group are left alone: their ticks and targets stay as they were.
- Nothing is removed. Running it again adds only new buffs — handy after a level up or a party change.
- Hidden buffs and buffs nobody can receive right now are skipped.
## Which buffs go to which group
- "Rounds" — rounds (per level or fixed).
- "Minutes (min/level)" — minutes per level.
- "10 min/level and longer" — 10 minutes per level, hours, days, permanent.
- "Hours and longer" — hours, days, permanent.
- "Toggles" — activatable abilities and songs.
- "Any duration" — no fill; buffs are added by hand with {A}.
The duration is taken from the effect. Without an exact duration, a long effect counts as hours and a short one as rounds. The duration column shows how the mod read the buff.
## How to use it
1. Open the group's buffs.
2. {Y} — fill. "added N" appears at the bottom.
3. Go through the list with {UP}{DOWN} and tick {X} the buffs to cast.
4. Remove the rest with {A} — or keep them unticked for later.
5. {RIGHT} on a buff — check who gets it.
> Why unticked: fill takes everything that matches, including what you don't need. You decide, so the group won't waste slots.

# Who gets the buff — automatically
When a buff is added to a group (by hand or by fill), the mod sets its targets based on how the buff is cast:
- **self** — the caster can cast it only on themselves (e.g. "Shield", "Mirror Image"). Everyone in the party who knows it gets it: each casts it on themselves.
- **party** — the buff can be cast on others. Its targets are everyone it can reach, pets included. Anyone who knows it and has a slot left casts it.
- **1 performer** — songs and performances. One performer starts it: the first one in the party.
Targets belong to the buff, not to the group: a buff in two groups goes to the same characters.
## When to adjust by hand
- A new companion gets no targets automatically. Open the Buffs tab and add them, or press {X} there to recalculate.
- Not everyone needs the buff — remove the extra targets in the Buffs tab.
- Removing the last target takes the buff out of every group.
- Giving a target to a buff that is in no group puts it into "{G1}".

# Buffs
The Buffs tab — who receives each buff. {RIGHT} on a buff in group buffs opens the same page.
The first row, **Show**, chooses which buffs are listed: "All", "Assigned" (those with targets) or a single group. {LEFT}{RIGHT} or {A} on it change the choice.
{UP}{DOWN}| select a buff; above the first one is the "Show" row.
{LEFT}{RIGHT}| select a character at the bottom.
{A}| make the character a target or not.
{Y}| whole party: everyone on, or everyone off.
{X}| auto targets: discard manual changes and set targets as when the buff was added (self / party / performer).
{B}| close the menu; from a group's buffs — back.
Green — the character gets the buff, yellow — the cursor.

# Settings
The Settings tab.
{UP}{DOWN}| select a row.
{A}| change; {LEFT}{RIGHT} — step a value back and forth.
{B}| close the menu.
## Casting
- **Allow buffing in combat** — the same as "Buffing in combat" in the Cast tab.
- **Cast all buffs on combat start** — when combat begins, cast every configured buff, as if each had "Cast on combat start".
- **Skip animations on combat start** — those casts go off at once.
- **Ignore existing buffs** — recast even on characters who already have the buff.
- **Use full animation casting** — every buff is cast with its full casting animation.
- WotR: **Bypass arcane spell failure when prebuffing** — outside combat, armor doesn't spoil the spell.
## Buff sources
Which sources the mod scans: songs and activatable abilities; in WotR also scrolls, potions and equipment, the order of sources and the Use Magic Device rules for scrolls. Changing them rescans the party's buffs.
## View
- **Hints** — auto (follows the game's control mode), gamepad buttons or keyboard keys.
- **Show hidden** — hidden buffs appear crossed out in the lists, so they can be shown again.
Hints, the bar position and "Show hidden" are shared by all playthroughs; everything else is stored per playthrough.

# Buff settings
Open: {RB} on a buff in group buffs.
- **Cast on combat start** — the buff is cast automatically when combat begins.
- **Deactivate after** — activatable abilities only: switch off after N combat rounds; 0 — no limit.
- **Hide ability** — the buff disappears from the lists; Settings › "Show hidden" brings it back.
- WotR: which sources this buff may use, the Extend Rod and the order of sources.
## Casters
Every caster of the buff, with its source:
- **Ban from casting** — this caster never casts the buff.
- **Limit casts to** — how many casts of this buff the caster may spend; the full number means no limit.
- **Priority (all buffs)** and **Priority (this buff)** — higher casts earlier.
- WotR: Share Transmutation, Powerful Change, Reservoir Caster Level and Azata Zippy Magic, where the caster has them.

# How casting works
- Only buffs ticked in this group are cast.
- Slots go first to the buffs of the group being cast.
- Targets that already have the buff are skipped.
- A buff in two groups is skipped when the second group is cast: it is already active.
- {X} in the Cast tab casts groups one after another: the next is planned after the previous one has spent its slots.
- In combat, groups don't start unless "Buffing in combat" is on.
## Messages
- **applied X/Y, already active Z** — X of Y attempts succeeded, Z targets already had it.
- **no caster** — the casters are out of slots; rest.
- **not started** — in combat with "Buffing in combat" off, or the group is already being cast.

# Example
A sample party: **Fighter**, **Cleric**, **Wizard**, **Bard**, **Rogue**. Spell names are just examples.
## After resting — "{G1}"
1. Groups › {A} on "{G1}" › {Y} fill.
2. Among the unticked additions: "Mage Armor" (hours, party), "Heroism" (10 min, party).
3. {X} on both. "Mage Armor" goes to all five — the Wizard casts it while slots last.
4. The Rogue doesn't need armor: {RIGHT} › {LEFT}{RIGHT} to the Rogue › {A}.
5. From now on, after every rest — {A} on "{G1}" in the Cast tab.
## Before a dangerous place — "{G2}"
- The Cleric's "Shield of Faith" — party: all five.
- The Wizard's "Shield" — self: only the Wizard.
- "Mirror Image", known by the Wizard and the Bard — self: each casts it on themselves.
## Before a boss — "{G3}"
- "Haste" — party, cast by the Wizard or the Bard.
- "Divine Power" — self, the Cleric.
- Fill won't add the song "Inspire Courage" here: its duration is "toggle". Find it in the grey list and press {A} — the Bard will perform it.
- Right before the fight — {A} on "{G3}" in the Cast tab.
## Own group "Against undead"
1. Groups › "+ New group" › type the name › {LB}{RB} "Any duration" › {Y}.
2. In its buffs: find "Protection from Evil" and "Death Ward" in the grey list › {A}.
3. The group appears in the Cast tab: {A} on it before entering the crypt.
## Switch a buff off for a while
No "Heroism" this time: Groups › {A} on "{G1}" › select "Heroism" › {X}. The tick is gone, the targets stay, and it still works in other groups.

# Where it is stored
Saved immediately in the mod's UserSettings folder: groups and buffs per playthrough, the menu's own settings for all playthroughs.

pad.help.km:
# Kingmaker
- Scrolls, potions, wands and charged items are switched on in Settings, under Sources; the order of sources is set there and per buff. The game itself rolls Use Magic Device: a failed check spends nothing and is rolled again up to the set number of times.
- An Extend rod works when it is in the caster's quick slot; it spends one of its daily charges.
- The cast result is shown in the pop-up and in the combat log.
- A slot is spent even when the spell fails (e.g. armor), as in the game itself.
- With mouse and keyboard the quick cast bar sits above the action bar; its position is set in Settings. Right click on a group button opens its buffs in this menu.
pad.help.src.end:
- only what applies a beneficial effect: attack and healing spells are not listed.
Remaining slots don't affect the list: a buff is shown with empty slots too and skipped at cast time with "no caster". Party and prepared spells are re-read on area load, party change and level up.
Order: the group's buffs alphabetically on top; below — the rest, those matching the group's duration first, then the others, each part alphabetically.
